updatePolicy.note: Sources are checked each month. Comparable official crime figures are released quarterly, usually about four months after the period ends.

categories.label: All recorded crime
categories.description: All notifiable police-recorded offences excluding fraud. Anti-social behaviour incidents are not included.

categories.label: Violence
categories.description: Violence against the person, including homicide, violence with and without injury, stalking and harassment. Recording practices affect comparisons.

categories.label: Sexual offences
categories.description: Police-recorded rape and other sexual offences. Changes in reporting and recording can affect trends.

categories.label: Robbery
categories.description: Theft involving force or the threat of force against a person, including personal and business property. An April 2025 clarification of police counting rules increased the recording of business robbery during shop theft involving violence or threats. Changes in robbery and shoplifting across this date can reflect the recording change as well as changes in crime.

categories.label: Burglary
categories.description: Residential and non-residential burglary. Rates use resident population, rather than the number of households.

categories.label: Vehicle crime
categories.description: Theft of and from vehicles, vehicle interference and related vehicle offences.

categories.label: Theft from the person
categories.description: Theft directly from a person without force or threat of force, including pickpocketing.

categories.label: Shoplifting
categories.description: Police-recorded theft from shops. Counts depend on offences being reported to and recorded by police. From April 2025, clarified counting rules require shop theft involving violence or threats, including during escape, to be recorded as business robbery. This can affect year-on-year shoplifting comparisons spanning that date.

categories.label: Criminal damage & arson
categories.description: Recorded criminal damage to property and arson offences.

categories.label: Drug offences
categories.description: Drug possession and trafficking offences. Recorded totals are influenced by police activity.

categories.label: Weapons possession
categories.description: Possession of weapons offences. This is not a count of all knife-enabled crime.

categories.label: Public order
categories.description: Police-recorded public order offences, including offences involving fear or provocation of violence.

categories.label: Homicide
categories.description: Police-recorded homicide offences, included within violence against the person. Percentage changes suppressed by ONS for small bases remain unavailable; a small absolute change can produce a large percentage change.

categories.label: Death or serious injury — unlawful driving
categories.description: Death or serious injury caused by unlawful driving, included within violence against the person. ONS small-base percentage-change suppressions are preserved.

categories.label: Violence with injury
categories.description: Recorded violence with injury, a component of violence against the person. Changes in reporting and crime recording can affect trends.

categories.label: Violence without injury
categories.description: Recorded violence without injury, a component of violence against the person. Stalking and harassment are shown separately.

categories.label: Stalking and harassment
categories.description: Recorded stalking and harassment, a component of violence against the person. Reporting and recording practices affect both levels and changes.

categories.label: All theft offences
categories.description: The parent total for burglary, vehicle offences, theft from the person, bicycle theft, shoplifting and other theft. These component categories must not be added to this total.

categories.label: Residential burglary
categories.description: A component of burglary, covering homes and other buildings within the boundary of a dwelling. The April 2023 split between homes and unconnected buildings does not change this combined total. Rates use residents, rather than households.

categories.label: Non-residential burglary
categories.description: Burglary of business and community premises, a component of total burglary and theft offences. Rates use the resident population.

categories.label: Bicycle theft
categories.description: Recorded theft of bicycles, a component of total theft offences.

categories.label: Other theft offences
categories.description: Other recorded theft offences, excluding the separately displayed burglary, vehicle offences, theft from the person, bicycle theft and shoplifting categories. A component of total theft offences.

categories.label: Miscellaneous crimes against society
categories.description: The Home Office miscellaneous crimes against society group, including offences such as handling stolen goods and perverting the course of justice. This completes the main offence-group breakdown.

categories.label: Knife-enabled crime
categories.description: Selected serious offences involving a knife or sharp instrument: homicide, attempted murder, threats to kill, assault with injury or intent to cause serious harm, robbery, rape and sexual assault. This overlaps violence, robbery and sexual offences; it is not weapons possession or a separate addition to all crime. Counts come from a separate collection. National totals include British Transport Police. History contains published annual observations and the latest equivalent rolling years, not quarterly estimates. Recording improvements, including NDQIS from April 2019, limit older comparisons; Greater Manchester data before its 2018 review and Metropolitan Police data before its April 2024 revisions are not directly comparable with later figures.

categories.label: Firearm offences
categories.description: Offences where a firearm was fired, used as a threat or used as a blunt instrument; conventional air weapons are excluded. This overlaps other offence categories and must not be added to all crime. It is not a count of shootings alone. National totals exclude British Transport Police. History contains published annual observations and the latest equivalent rolling years. Recording improvements limit historical comparisons; the Metropolitan Police changed systems in February 2024 and revised figures from April 2024.

notes: The England and Wales reference includes British Transport Police except for firearm offences. Regional and territorial-force comparisons exclude it. London regional totals include City of London.

Main offence groups and their detailed components overlap. Knife-enabled and firearm offences also overlap other categories. Never add parent groups, their components and weapon-enabled measures together.
Published ONS percentage-change suppressions are preserved, including small-base suppressions. Some observations have counts but no published comparable change.

Standard offence histories contain quarterly rolling-year totals. Knife-enabled and firearm histories retain the actual published annual dates and latest equivalent rolling years; intervening quarterly observations are not estimated. Historical weapon rates are unavailable before a matching ONS population estimate exists.

An April 2025 clarification of police counting rules increased the recording of business robbery during shop theft involving violence or threats. Changes in robbery and shoplifting across this date can reflect the recording change as well as changes in crime.
methodology: Counts describe police-recorded crime, rather than every crime that occurs. Reporting levels, recording practices and police activity affect comparisons and trends.
Each count covers a rolling 12-month period. Year-on-year change compares the count with the preceding rolling year ending in the same quarter.
Fraud and anti-social behaviour incidents are excluded. Weapons possession is not the same measure as knife-enabled crime.

Rates are calculated from exact ONS mid-year resident-population estimates, not inferred from rounded published rates. Historical rates use the latest available estimate at or before the year preceding each period end. Historical population estimates may be revised.

Standard crime histories sum four consecutive quarters from the latest Home Office revised open-data file. Latest and previous-year counts are reconciled against ONS Tables P1 and P4, and published percentage changes/suppressions against P2, before publication. Knife totals reconcile between P5 and P6 and current rates against P7; firearm counts and their dated histories come directly from P8.
City of London counts remain visible, but its resident-based rates and rate rankings are suppressed. London regional totals include City of London.
This version covers England and Wales. Crime recording systems and offence definitions differ in Scotland and Northern Ireland.
